value: receives the recovered quote and token of the dying generation through `_removeLiquidity` (line 804); burns the recovered dead-generation tokens with `burn` (line 811); pulls the hook reserves and the dying vault inside `seedFunding` (line 948); pays the whole funded amount into the newborn pool through `_seedGeneration` (line 1065)
reachability: Permissionless in the caller dimension but heavily state-gated. Four preconditions must hold before anything moves: the machine must have been ignited (`summoned` CauldronRegistry.sol:772), the hook must judge the live pool dead (`isDead` CauldronRegistry.sol:779), the grace clock must have expired (`minLifetime` CauldronRegistry.sol:783), and a governor must be wired AND holding proposals (`hasProposals` CauldronRegistry.sol:787). The generation counter advances at `currentGeneration` CauldronRegistry.sol:839 and the grace clock restarts at `lastSummonAt` CauldronRegistry.sol:840, before the new token exists. The proposer-supplied quote is narrowed twice and never allowed to revert: the allowlist re-check at `allowedQuote` CauldronRegistry.sol:897, then the mining fallback inside `_deployToken` CauldronRegistry.sol:916, then the funding narrowing in `seedFunding` CauldronRegistry.sol:948. `markConsumed` CauldronRegistry.sol:977 is placed after the only remaining revert, the zero-funding check at `totalETH` CauldronRegistry.sol:976, so the fatal window in which a revert would roll the consumption back is short. The quote actually achieved is recorded at `generationQuote` CauldronRegistry.sol:982 and the funding figure it is denominated in comes from the PRIMARY pair's currency0 at `generationPoolKey` CauldronRegistry.sol:951, not from the generation-quote mapping. Reserve sizing folds the pending OG share in at `genesisPending` CauldronRegistry.sol:1001, clamps three ways at `newActive` CauldronRegistry.sol:1016, CauldronRegistry.sol:1043 and CauldronRegistry.sol:1056, and only then splits supply at `newReserve` CauldronRegistry.sol:1057. Iteration two branches into the continuation path at `mifrens` CauldronRegistry.sol:1072; every other iteration deploys a fresh collection at `_deployCollection` CauldronRegistry.sol:1075. Two sub-calls are gas-capped against the tail reserve, the ticket drain at `RELAUNCH_TAIL_RESERVE` CauldronRegistry.sol:821 and the perp force-close at `RELAUNCH_TAIL_RESERVE` CauldronRegistry.sol:1125.
observations: comment at `Permissionless` CauldronRegistry.sol:759 says anyone can call once the pool is confirmed dead; code at `hasProposals` CauldronRegistry.sol:787 additionally requires a wired governor holding proposals, and `minLifetime` CauldronRegistry.sol:783 additionally requires the grace period to have elapsed.

comment at `NEVER` CauldronRegistry.sol:797 says a revert in the force-close step can never brick the rebirth; code at `forceClosePerps` CauldronRegistry.sol:1126 makes that call without a try/catch, and the note at `WRAPPED` CauldronRegistry.sol:1107 states the opposite, that letting it revert rolls the whole rebirth back.

comment at `CREATE` CauldronRegistry.sol:915 says the new generation's token is deployed with plain CREATE; code reached from `_deployToken` CauldronRegistry.sol:916 deploys it with CREATE2 from a mined salt at `salt` PoolOps.sol:707, using plain CREATE only in the unmined fallback at `CauldronToken` PoolOps.sol:718.

reachability: Private, reached only from the two calls inside the rebirth at `_perpHousekeep` CauldronRegistry.sol:801 and CauldronRegistry.sol:1085. The two branches are not symmetric in failure handling: the sync branch swallows everything in a try/catch at `syncGeneration` CauldronRegistry.sol:1097, while the force-close branch calls `forceClosePerps` CauldronRegistry.sol:1126 bare, so a revert there propagates and rolls the whole relaunch back. Both are gas-capped, the close against `RELAUNCH_TAIL_RESERVE` CauldronRegistry.sol:1125, and the engine address is read off the hook rather than stored here (`perpEngine` CauldronRegistry.sol:1096). When the cap check fails because `g` CauldronRegistry.sol:1125 is below the reserve, the close is skipped entirely and the rebirth continues with the book untouched (DERIVED).

Private; reached from ignition at `_deployCollection` CauldronRegistry.sol:743 and from every non-continuation rebirth at CauldronRegistry.sol:1075. It cannot revert on missing metadata because an empty base URI falls back to a literal at `baseURI` CauldronRegistry.sol:1147 and a zero cap falls back to `nftMaxSupply` CauldronRegistry.sol:1149. The factory call at `deployBrew` CauldronRegistry.sol:1151 is NOT wrapped, so a broken or unset factory reverts the whole rebirth (DERIVED). The hook is then repointed at the new collection (`setCollection` CauldronRegistry.sol:1167) and its vault sink is deliberately zeroed (`setVault` CauldronRegistry.sol:1171), routing the floor share into the token buyback instead.

Private and reachable exactly once in the machine's life, from the iteration-two branch at `_continueMiFrens` CauldronRegistry.sol:1073, which requires `mifrens` CauldronRegistry.sol:1072 to be wired. No new collection is deployed; only a fresh floor vault at `deployVault` CauldronRegistry.sol:1189, whose offset is `genesisShares` CauldronRegistry.sol:1189 so the forged tranche cannot draw the OG floor. It then takes over the canonical collection by pointing its minter at the hook (`setMinter` CauldronRegistry.sol:1193), which requires this registry to already hold that authority on the collection (DERIVED).

reachability: Open to any holder of a strictly earlier generation (`currentGeneration` CauldronRegistry.sol:1229). When a vesting escrow is configured the direct path is closed to everyone except the escrow itself and the perp engine (`claimGate` CauldronRegistry.sol:1234). The source generation must be known (`prevToken` CauldronRegistry.sol:1238) and the caller must actually hold the amount (`balanceOf` CauldronRegistry.sol:1239). It deliberately carries no reentrancy guard, which is what lets the engine migrate its inventory while the rebirth already holds the lock (`migrateOne` CauldronRegistry.sol:1244). The release is strict: a reserve that cannot cover the amount reverts and un-burns atomically.

reachability: Same gating as the strict form: an earlier generation only (`currentGeneration` CauldronRegistry.sol:1267) and the escrow exemption at `claimGate` CauldronRegistry.sol:1268. The difference is the sizing: the request is first clamped to the caller's balance at `bal` CauldronRegistry.sol:1275 and then, inside `migrateUpTo` CauldronRegistry.sol:1279, to whatever the reserve can actually deliver, so it returns a partial fill instead of reverting. It exists so the perp engine's whole-book sync cannot revert inside its own try/catch (DERIVED).
